wrong: Philippines
The Philippines has one national police force, the PNP, under the DILG.
New Zealand
New Zealand has a single national police force.
Ireland
Ireland has a single national police force, the Garda Siochana.
Many independent local police forces
That is a decentralized system.
Police controlled by each city mayor
Local control by mayors is a feature of decentralized systems.
Separate federal, state and local forces

wrong: Speedy arrest of any suspect
Speed of arrest is not due process; due process is fair treatment under the law.
Immediate punishment upon arrest
Punishment without trial violates due process.
Trial held only after a confession
A confession is not required for trial, and forcing one violates due process.

wrong: Installing cameras at every entrance
That is a countermeasure, chosen after the risks are assessed.
Hiring more guards for each shift
That is a countermeasure, not the assessment itself.
Buying insurance to cover any losses after an incident
That is risk transfer, one way of handling a risk once it has been assessed.
Questionnaire on employee job satisfaction
That is an employee survey, not a security survey.
Inspection of fire exits by the fire bureau
That is a fire safety inspection by the BFP.
Inventory of the company's guards and equipment
An inventory lists resources; a security survey assesses vulnerabilities.
Guarding the outer fence
That is perimeter security.
Securing computer files
That is information security.
Escorting company executives
That is personal (executive) security.
Protection of the building's interior rooms
That is interior security.
Protection of VIPs
That is personal security.
Protection of data and records
That is information security.
Pan-pan
Pan-pan is the urgency signal, one level below distress.
Securite
Securite is the safety signal, used for navigation or weather warnings.
Roger
Roger only means the message was received.
Strict enforcement of every law without exception
That is full enforcement, which leaves no room for discretion.
Following orders without any personal judgment
Discretion is the officer's own judgment, not mechanical obedience.
Decisions made by the police chief for all officers
Discretion belongs to the individual officer in the situation.

wrong: Visible patrol to deter crime
Patrol is visible presence; surveillance is close, usually covert observation.
Questioning a suspect in custody
That is interrogation.
Briefing the press on a case
That is public information work, not surveillance.
Intelligence from intercepted signals
That is SIGINT.
Intelligence from photos and imagery
That is IMINT, or imagery intelligence.
Public-source intelligence
That is OSINT, or open-source intelligence.
Intelligence gathered from informants and agents
That is HUMINT.
Intelligence gathered from satellite and aerial images
That is IMINT, or imagery intelligence.
Intelligence gathered from newspapers and websites
That is OSINT, or open-source intelligence.
Record of who handled the evidence
That is the chain of custody.
Order of promotion by seniority
Promotion order is a personnel matter, not the chain of command.
Radio network linking all units
That is the communication system.
Each subordinate reports to only one superior
That is unity of command.
Limit on how many people one can supervise
That is span of control.
Grouping of similar tasks into units
That is specialization, or functional grouping.

wrong: Authority flows in a line from top to bottom
That is the scalar principle.
A supervisor oversees only a set number of people
That is span of control.
Decisions are shared by all team members equally
That is participative decision-making, not unity of command.
Reporting to only one superior
That is unity of command.
Line of authority from top to bottom
That is the scalar principle.
Area covered by a patrol beat
That is the beat area, not span of control.

wrong: Several supervisors per subordinate
That violates unity of command.
Fixed number of people per supervisor
That is span of control.
Team without any supervisor
Unity of command requires each person to have a supervisor.
Patrol moving in no fixed pattern around the beat
That is random patrol.
Patrol following the same route every shift
That is routine patrol, which is predictable.
Patrol done only when citizens call for help
That is reactive response to calls, not directed patrol.
Barangay police patrol of the community
That describes the barangay tanods.
Municipal court for minor criminal cases
That is the Municipal Trial Court.
Barangay council that passes local ordinances
That is the Sangguniang Barangay.
Patrol covering every street equally
Selective patrol concentrates where crime analysis points, not evenly.
Patrol with no fixed route
That is random patrol.
Patrol only at night
Selective patrol follows crime data, not a fixed time of day.
Transfer from another agency at the same rank
That is a transfer, not lateral entry.
Entry at the lowest rank after basic training
That is regular entry, the opposite of lateral entry.
Temporary hiring during elections or emergencies
That is temporary or emergency hiring.
Increase in personnel through new hiring
That is recruitment, the opposite of attrition.
Movement of officers to other units
That is transfer.
Advancement of officers to higher ranks
That is promotion.

Room where suspects are held before they are questioned

Permit to carry a firearm outside residence

Release order for a detained person
